correctness.rationale: For X=IG(k,2n), 1<=k<=n, the Plucker degree formula follows from the leading Weyl-dimension coefficient with dimension d=k(4n-3k+1)/2; Bruhat cells give chi=2^k binomial(n,k). The printed proof compares R=deg/chi by an explicit strictly positive polynomial for n->n+1 at fixed k>=2. At n=k, LG(k,2k) normalized degrees are strictly increasing for k>=3 after L3=16; k=2 crosses between n=2 (2<4) and n=3 (14>12). Thus equality never occurs. Independently recomputed type-C coroot product, factorial degree and Euler count up to n=16, plus strict cases; finite checks are regression, not the infinite argument.

evidence: General Weyl character formulas imply the separate degree calculation, but do not without the displayed growth inequalities imply its strict ordering against 2^k binomial(n,k).
